Snapshot of account: mid-market e-commerce returns platform; heavy emphasis on automated refunds and ticket management. Primary ask: build agent-assist + automated ticket-create/update flows that can call payment provider APIs (Stripe/Adyen) and Zendesk Service APIs to create refunds and escalate to ops with full audit trail. Key technical constraints: PCI-sensitive payloads (tokenize payment info), KMS-managed keys, retention controls for transcripts, and regional data residency (want EU for EU customers).

Tech notes (from 2026-02-18 call):
- They want tool-calls to support: create/update Zendesk tickets, create refund transactions (Stripe refund API), escalate to Level 2 with metadata and conversation snapshot.
- Concern: duplicate refunds if retried; ask for idempotency token patterns and reconciliation process. Quote from head of ops: "We cannot tolerate double refunds — that's our biggest fear."
- Spike reliability: expected 5-10x peaks during promotional returns windows. Need autoscaling + graceful degradation (fallback to queueing + user-visible state).
- Observability: require per-token/call cost breakdown, per-route latency SLOs, and searchable audit logs for tool-calls with replay/forensics.
- Security asks: SSO (SAML), SOC2 evidence, KMS integration for key rotation, audit logging retention 7 years for disputed refunds, and regional hosting for EU customers.
- Integrations: Zendesk for ticketing, Stripe for refunds (PCI tokens), internal ERP (webhooks) for settlement reconciliation.

POC ask: Redwood to run 2-week POC that includes:
1) scripted 10x spike (synthetic traffic) validating latency and success rate for ticket-create+refund workflow;
2) tests for idempotent retries (simulate network failures and webhook retries);
3) demo of audit logs and per-call traceability;
4) security review including KMS integration and data residency proof-of-concept.

Operational notes: AE Priya to coordinate legal & payments teams, SE Liam to prepare integration playbook and idempotency pattern doc, CSM Renee to draft onboarding checklist if POC passes. Drive links sent for pricing and security FAQ. Jira SUP-4312 created for demo defects.
concise_use_case_summary: Agent-assist + automated tool-calls to create/update tickets and issue refunds. Must guarantee idempotency for money actions, maintain full auditability, and survive 10x traffic spikes with graceful degradation (queueing/circuit-breaker).
preferred_models_and_routing: Prefer smaller specialized models for NLU + a verified RL/LLM for summarization; want ability to route high-risk actions (refunds/escalations) through a private deployment lane (VPC) with automatic fallback to dedicated hosted models for non-sensitive tasks.
pricing_sensitivity_and_expectations: Cost-sensitive on per-refund basis; willing to pay premium for private/dedicated lanes that guarantee audit logs and KMS-managed keys. Expect ARR in 50k-120k band first year with growth if reliability metrics met.
escalation_playbook_requirements: Must support synchronous tool-calls for ticket creation and asynchronous fallback (persist-to-queue + operator alert) when downstream payment API unavailable. Require webhooks for settlement reconciliation and SLA on retry/backoff behavior.
